questions.q: What are the male gametes produced in the human reproductive system called?
What are the female gametes produced in the human ovaries called?
Where are male sperm cells produced in the human body?
What is the function of the scrotum surrounding the testes?
a: To keep the testes at a slightly lower temperature than core body temperature, which is optimal for sperm production

questions.q: What is the tube that carries sperm from the testes to the urethra during ejaculation?
What do the prostate gland and seminal vesicles contribute to the reproductive system?
a: They secrete fluids containing nutrients and mucus (semen) to nourish and transport sperm

questions.q: Where does fertilization of an egg cell by a sperm cell normally take place in the female reproductive system?
What is the muscular organ where a fertilized egg implants and develops into a fetus during pregnancy?
What is the ring of muscle at the lower opening of the uterus that dilates during childbirth called?
What is ovulation defined as?
a: The fusion of sperm and egg
The release of a mature egg cell from an ovary into the oviduct
The shedding of the uterine lining during menstruation
The implantation of an embryo into the uterus wall

questions.q: What is the average length of a normal human menstrual cycle?
Which hormone is released by the pituitary gland to stimulate the development of an egg follicle in the ovary?
Which hormone is responsible for repairing and thickening the lining of the uterus during the first half of the menstrual cycle?
What triggers ovulation around day 14 of the menstrual cycle?
a: A surge in Luteinizing Hormone (LH) from the pituitary gland

questions.q: What is the function of the corpus luteum formed after ovulation?
a: To secrete progesterone and some oestrogen, maintaining the thick uterine lining

questions.q: What happens to the uterine lining if fertilization does not occur?
a: It thickens further into placenta tissue
It is absorbed completely by white blood cells
It breaks down and is shed along with blood during menstruation

questions.q: What is implantation?
a: The embedding of a fertilized embryo into the thick lining (endometrium) of the uterus
The release of an egg from the ovary
The swimming of sperm up the oviduct

questions.q: What is the role of the placenta during pregnancy?
a: To allow exchange of nutrients, oxygen, and waste products (like urea and carbon dioxide) between maternal and fetal blood without their blood supplies mixing directly
To pump fetal blood through the mother's body
To act as a skeletal support for the fetus

questions.q: What is the function of the amniotic sac and amniotic fluid surrounding the fetus?
a: To provide oxygen directly to fetal lungs
To digest food for the fetus
To protect the fetus from physical shocks and mechanical injury by cushioning it

questions.q: Which of the following describes a barrier method of birth control (contraception)?
a: Condom or diaphragm, which physically prevents sperm from reaching the egg

questions.q: What is the purpose of hormonal contraceptives (such as the birth control pill)?
a: To suppress ovulation by preventing the release of FSH and LH, or altering cervical mucus
To kill all bacteria in the vagina

questions.q: What is a Sexually Transmitted Infection (STI) caused by a bacterium or virus?
a: An infection transmitted primarily through sexual contact (e.g., HIV, Gonorrhea, Syphilis, Chlamydia)
A genetic disorder inherited from parents
A nutritional deficiency disease like scurvy

questions.q: How does the human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) affect the human body?
a: It infects and destroys immune system white blood cells (lymphocytes), eventually leading to AIDS

questions.q: Which of the following methods of contraception is considered permanent and irreversible?
a: Surgical sterilization (tubal ligation in females or vasectomy in males)

questions.q: What adaptations do sperm cells have that help them reach and fertilize an egg?
a: A flagellum (tail) for swimming, a haploid nucleus, and an acrosome containing enzymes to digest the egg membrane
A large food store and thick protective cell wall

questions.q: How is an egg cell (ovum) structurally adapted for fertilization and early development?
a: It is microscopic and has a tail
It is much larger than sperm, contains a food energy store (cytoplasm), and has a jelly coat that changes after fertilization to block other sperm

questions.q: What is the difference between a zygote and a fetus?
a: A zygote is born; a fetus is an egg
A fetus is single-celled; a zygote is multi-celled
A zygote is the single cell formed immediately after fertilization; a fetus is the later stage of prenatal development with recognizable organ systems

questions.q: Which STI is caused by a bacterium and can be successfully treated and cured using antibiotics such as penicillin?
What is the role of testosterone in human males besides sperm production?
a: It stimulates the development of male secondary sexual characteristics during puberty (e.g., facial hair, deepening voice, muscle growth)
It triggers the breakdown of the uterus lining
It stimulates milk production in breasts

questions.q: What is puberty?
a: The process of aging in elderly adults
The period during which adolescents reach sexual maturity and become capable of reproduction
The cessation of menstrual cycles in women

questions.q: Why do maternal and fetal blood supplies not mix directly inside the placenta?
a: To prevent the fetus from breathing air
To allow blood pressure to drop
To protect the delicate fetal capillaries from high maternal blood pressure and prevent certain pathogens or incompatible blood cells from crossing directly
To keep fetal blood at a higher temperature

questions.q: What is the function of the umbilical cord connecting the fetus to the placenta?
a: To pump blood using fetal muscles
To contain blood vessels (umbilical artery and vein) transporting blood between the fetus and the placenta

questions.q: Which female hormone inhibits the release of FSH and stimulates the pituitary gland to release LH during the menstrual cycle?
What is the primary cause of infertility in females related to ovulation?
a: Failure to release eggs (ovulation) or blocked oviducts

questions.q: How can barrier methods of contraception also help reduce the risk of STIs?
a: They kill all bacteria in the blood
They vaccinate the body against viruses
They physically block the exchange of bodily fluids containing pathogens between partners
They increase white blood cell count

questions.q: What is the name of the fluid ejaculated by the male containing sperm and secretions from accessory glands?
